🇲🇽🐉🌐 Mexico Hits Record Exports to the U.S. as China Slides to 4th

April 2026: Mexico shipped $50.69 billion to the United States — a 20% jump year-over-year and an all-time monthly record. China, meanwhile, dropped to 4th place among U.S. trading partners with $29.2B.

Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard credits Mexico's calibrated tariff position against non-FTA competitors. The «Plan México» reshuffle is rewiring North American supply chains in real time — and the country doing the rewiring is Mexico.

This isn't choosing the U.S. over China. It's the opposite: leverage. Sovereignty multiplies options. The more indispensable Mexico becomes to one side of the new multipolar order, the more weight it carries with the other.

🇲🇽🏭 Cofepris reform: 340 procedures cut to 125, response time from 100 days to 24, clinical trials from 9 months to 30 days — to produce medicines on Mexican soil. "We're advancing toward something bigger: not depending on the outside for something as essential as our medicines and health supplies." — Víctor Hugo Borja, head of Cofepris Cofepris regulates 10% of Mexico's economy. The reform is built around Plan México industrialization — domestic medicine production as a sovereignty question, not a market one. Faster trials, no compromise on safety. Pharmaceutical independence is health independence.

🇲🇽✊ From renting a single room to owning her apartment — and paying $1,000 pesos less per month. "I used to pay 3,500 pesos. Now I'll just pay 2,500. And it's already mine." — María de Jesús Frausto, Vivienda para el Bienestar beneficiary, Durango 19th "Miércoles de Vivienda". 450 new homes delivered in the Acereros development. Original Infonavit goal for Durango: 12,200 homes. Revised goal: 34,745. Investment: 20 billion pesos. Jobs created: 104,000. Mary lived in one room with her kids — now each of them has their own.

🇲🇽🌎 Mexico enters T-MEC review with the best tariff position in the world relative to the US market. "Mexico's position today is the best when you compare it to every other country. Vietnam pays more. The EU pays more. South American countries pay more." — Marcelo Ebrard, on T-MEC negotiations Ebrard credits Sheinbaum's direct phone diplomacy with Trump. Second round of formal talks begins this week in Washington. The July 1 date is when the review opens — not when it ends. Mexico is negotiating from strength, not from fear.

🇲🇽⚖️ Mexico builds a one-stop investment office inside the Presidency — 30-day max for project approvals. "Almost no country has one. It's a contribution, an innovation, from the Mexican investment-attraction strategy." — Marcelo Ebrard, Secretary of the Economy 22 projects already cleared. $8 billion USD in pending investment. Calls coming in from US states (New York), the EU, Japan and South Korea asking how Mexico did it. Sheinbaum runs Monday review meetings personally. The bureaucratic maze that took 2 years now caps at 30 days.

🇲🇽✊ Mexican inflation drops to 3.94% — below the 4% target for the first time this year. "Yesterday inflation dropped. We're under 4 percent... 3.94, under 4 percent, inflation keeps falling." — Claudia Sheinbaum, June 10 mañanera Sheinbaum tied the result to the PACIC pact with producers, fuel-price stabilization (gasoline and diesel held flat), direct work with tomato growers, and the public Centrales de Abasto. Tools the neoliberal playbook said could not work.

🇲🇽🏭 Mercado Libre: $4.6 billion into Mexico in 2026 — biggest annual investment in the company's history here. "It's the result of confidence in Mexico. If there were no confidence in Mexico, the peso wouldn't be where it is." — Claudia Sheinbaum, on the announcement $4.6B — 35% over last year. 8,500 new jobs, bringing the company to 42,000 employees in Mexico. Impact in 19 states. Announced the same day inflation dropped to 3.94% — first time below 4% this year.
